newsitem.title: TURKEY: Ten dead in Turkey's Kurd conflict.
newsitem.headline: Ten dead in Turkey's Kurd conflict.

text.p: Security forces have killed eight Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) guerrillas in recent clashes in which one soldier died and two were wounded in southeast Turkey, military officials said on Tuesday.
Troops killed six PKK guerillas late on Monday in Aktuluk village in Turkey's mountainous Tunceli province in an operation to seek out the rebels, a military official told Reuters.
One soldier was killed in a rebel ambush in Doludizgin village in the same province, the official said, without saying when exactly the clash took place.
A further two guerrillas were killed and two soldiers were wounded in separate fighting over the weekend in the Kutuderesi ravine in Tunceli, he said.
The state-run Anatolian news agency reported the funeral of one soldier killed in fighting with the rebels in Bingol province, east of Tunceli. It did not say when he was killed.
The clashes occurred as Turkish troops kept up a six-week cross-border offensive against PKK positions into northern Iraq which the rebels have used to launch attacks into Turkey.
More than 24,000 people have been killed in the 12-year conflict between the troops and the PKK, fighting for autonomy or self-rule in Turkey's mainly Kurdish southeast.
